chapter: Touring abroad and the future of music
title: Why he distrusts the music educators' convention
summary: Herman says that the jazz educators' organisation has not helped real problems, citing egos he met, and he will not make a speech there.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Uh --
I'd like all these big music conventions and all this bullshit that happens in America where I've never really been, I've never been asked to attend, and I probably will never go --
Well, you're going to this convention in --

Oh, yeah, because we were bought to play. But I'm not going there as a person who's interested in what they're into, because I don't think they've ever come close to the real problems of the music industry, educational part of it or any part of it. They're still deciding who they like and don't like. They're doing the critique, and that's bullshit.
Would you like to have a platform to say
something about that, at that convention of --
No, because I don't think I want to. It's much to late for me and I don't think they'd understand what I was talking about.
I never saw such terrible ego as the few people I ever met from that organization, sick egos.
Is that right?
I remember when the jazz educators asked me if I was a member. I said, 'What is it?' And they told me, 'Well, if you would join you pay the tuition or whatever it is, you can become a member.'
I'd like for them to know about that, but I don't want to make any speech because I don't think they'd understand me.
No, I was just thinking about this discussion for helping them with their direction, really --
No, I think that it's too late. But I'll be glad if someone wanted to have a question and answer period, I'll be glad to answer their questions.
Yeah. I was just thinking about it, because you'll be there, and I should think there's a new echelon, new members of the top echelon --
I met only a very sketchy few of the old, and I certainly (unintelligible) was turned off.
Well, that's one of the reasons I was talking to some of the people. I think there's a new perspec-
tive coming around.
Well, I think these are things they should be made aware of, whether it's by me or somebody else. You could make them aware.
Yeah, I'm taking stock of all that stuff.

But I really have a hate thing going on about it. Like, if we can allow this country to do this to our music, that's completely -- the last one of our messages that should mean something. What the hell else do we have going?
